category_part_name: Introduction
quote_original: The immediate aftermath of World War II was characterized by a rapid transition from global conflict to a sophisticated state of geopolitical maneuvering, where the acquisition of strategic raw materials became a cornerstone of national security. Operation Highjump, officially designated as the United States Navy Antarctic Developments Project, 1946–1947, and organized as Task Force 68, represents one of the most ambitious manifestations of this new strategic reality.

category_part_name: The Institutional Architecture of Resource Appraisal (1944–1947)
quote_original:
Between the fiscal years of 1939–1940 and 1945–1946, the USGS experienced an unprecedented expansion, more than doubling its available funds from $7.5 million to over $15.1 million. This budgetary surge was accompanied by a nearly 70% increase in non-seasonal staff, growing from 1,472 to more than 2,490 scientists and engineers. This expanded capacity was specifically directed toward identifying strategic minerals, a mission that converged with the military objectives of the U.S. Navy as the Cold War began to take shape.
